summary: Over the last 4 weeks training volume has been very low and inconsistent — only 10 sessions recorded across all three disciplines, with no running at all and sleep chronically short (many nights under 5 hours, several under 4 hours). Body battery readings are generally moderate-to-low (peaking at 80 on one day), confirming accumulated fatigue from poor sleep rather than training overload. With the Half Oceanman 5,000m swim just 14 days away, the priority is arriving fresh: swim confidence is building (2km open-water sessions at avg ~160bpm), but the current plan's long ride and long run this weekend still carry meaningful fatigue risk.
suggestions: Sleep is your biggest limiter right now — chronically short nights (several under 4 hours) are suppressing recovery and adaptation far more than any training tweak; prioritise 7–8 hours nightly this week above all else.

Your open-water swim pace (~28–31 min/km) is slower than your 2:30/100m race target (~25 min/km); add one focused pool session this coming week with 100m pace reps to rehearse race rhythm before the taper begins.

Cap this Saturday's long ride at 60–75 minutes of easy Z2 (no threshold work) and Sunday's long run at 10–12km easy — the plan already flags these reductions and they are the right call with 13–14 days to race day.

Avoid the Wk14 Thursday cycling intervals (5×5min @ Z4 Threshold, 210–244W) entirely — at 10 days out from the Half Oceanman, threshold bike work creates residual fatigue without improving race-day fitness in the swim.

In the 2–3 days immediately after the Half Oceanman (Oct 3–5) before the Treviso 10K build resumes, take full rest rather than jumping back into the long run planned for Oct 4 — post-race recovery protects your 10K legs.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk13 Long Ride (AI adjusted) — 60km @ 120–145W, cap at 120 min
proposed_changes.proposed_session: 60–70 min easy Z2 spin at 120–140W, flat terrain, perceived effort only — no distance target, stop at first sign of fatigue.
proposed_changes.reason: 13 days out from the Half Oceanman with chronically poor sleep, even a 120-min capped ride accumulates meaningful leg fatigue; 60–70 min preserves aerobic stimulus while protecting freshness.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk13 Long Run (AI adjusted) — 10–12km @ 6:45–7:00/km, cap at 75 min
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Easy 8–10km run at 6:45–7:15/km, HR ≤135bpm, walk-break if needed — cap at 55 minutes and stop early if legs feel heavy from yesterday's ride.
proposed_changes.reason: 12 days before the swim race a 75-min run remains higher than necessary; reducing to 55 min ensures the athlete enters race week with fully recovered legs and no added DOMS risk.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk14 Pool Swim (Tuesday) — 2km+ technique drills and aerobic sets at ≤2:30/100m
proposed_changes.proposed_session: 2,000m pool session focused on race-pace rehearsal: 400m warm-up, 8×100m @ 2:25–2:30/100m with 20s rest, 400m cool-down — total ~2,000m; note the race-pace feel in each rep.
proposed_changes.reason: Open-water data shows current pace is 28–31 min/km vs the 2:30/100m race target; a structured 100m pace-rep set this week is the single highest-value session before taper begins.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk14 Evening session — 5×5min @ 210–244W (Z4 Threshold) intervals, 60–75 min total
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Skip entirely — convert to full rest or a maximum 20-min easy legs-out spin at 90–110W, no intervals whatsoever.
proposed_changes.reason: Z4 threshold cycling 9 days before the Half Oceanman adds residual muscular fatigue with zero race-specific benefit for a swim event; rest here is worth more than fitness.

proposed_changes.proposed_session: 45–60 min easy Z2 spin at 128–150W on flat roads — this is race week (7 days out); volume drops sharply and no tempo blocks.
proposed_changes.reason: A 4-hour, 120km ride 7 days before the Half Oceanman would leave meaningful fatigue in the legs and cardiovascular system right at the point taper should be at its deepest.

proposed_changes.proposed_session: Full rest day — no running. Athlete raced the Half Oceanman 5,000m swim on Oct 3; allow 48 hours of passive recovery before resuming any training ahead of the Treviso 10K on Oct 10.
proposed_changes.reason: Running 21.5km the day after a 5,000m open-water race risks injury and suppresses recovery at exactly the wrong time with the Treviso 10K only 6 days later.
